final_candidates.decision_summary: M1775R is a focused perturbation in the terminal BRCT region, expected to strongly disrupt BRCT-dependent recognition and repair functions while avoiding truncation or direct disruption of the N-terminal RING zinc-binding core.

K1702E reverses charge at a C-terminal BRCT-region functional surface, plausibly disabling an essential interaction or recognition determinant with lower global-folding risk than mutations of metal-coordinating residues.
R1699Q removes a key charged side-chain feature in the BRCT region and is expected to impair critical recognition or local functional architecture while retaining the complete protein sequence.

stop_reason.detail: The candidate pool has converged on selectively disruptive BRCT-region substitutions, and no external evidence is available to justify further reranking.

history.rationale: S1655 lies in the C-terminal BRCT phosphopeptide-recognition region; removing its hydroxyl should impair ligand-dependent DNA-repair signaling without introducing a major steric disruption.

Ser1655 lies in the C-terminal BRCT region and alanine substitution is expected to remove a potentially essential recognition-side-chain contribution with a relatively conservative structural perturbation.
This is a conservative-size but chemistry-removing change in the terminal functional region, offering a plausible functional knockout without global destabilization.
Removing this serine may impair a local regulatory or binding determinant, but the functional consequence is less certain than the top BRCT candidates.

K1702 is a key basic residue in the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding pocket. Alanine substitution is expected to remove binding chemistry while being comparatively compatible with the folded BRCT scaffold.
A charge-removing substitution at Lys1702 is a plausible way to disrupt BRCT-mediated molecular recognition while retaining a compact side chain and avoiding a grossly destabilizing deletion.
Removing a lysine side-chain charge may disrupt a local functional contact while being less likely than a disruptive core mutation to unfold the full protein.
Alanine removal of Lys1702 is a milder alternative to charge reversal and is retained as a lower-risk but potentially lower-impact perturbation.
Replacing K1702 with a neutral hydrophobic residue should strongly disrupt recognition of phosphorylated partner peptides while avoiding a truncation or cysteine/zinc-coordination defect.
Methionine is less structurally conservative than alanine and may introduce hydrophobic packing effects, so it is retained below K1702A despite potentially eliminating the same basic interaction.
Replacing Lys with a hydrophobic methionine removes charge and hydrogen-bonding capacity, but is less targeted than alanine or glutamate at this position.
Methionine removes lysine charge but has an uncertain local packing effect, making it less interpretable than K1702E or K1702A.

A bulky aromatic substitution at S1655 should block the local phosphopeptide-binding geometry and may more completely disable BRCT-mediated repair recruitment than a conservative deletion of the hydroxyl.
Phenylalanine should strongly disrupt the local polar recognition chemistry, but its bulk creates greater risk of damaging BRCT-domain packing than S1655A.
The bulky hydrophobic replacement could disrupt a local recognition surface, although it has higher folding risk than S1655A.
A bulky aromatic replacement could disrupt the local region, but carries more risk of nonspecific local destabilization than S1655A.
R1699 is within the first BRCT repeat and changing its positive side chain to glutamine may weaken functional partner recognition with less drastic disruption than core-destabilizing BRCT mutations.
Arg1699-to-Gln removes a charged side chain in the BRCT region and could impair functional interactions, although the degree of fold preservation is uncertain.
Neutralization of a charged residue in the terminal functional region is a plausible interface perturbation, but its functional consequence is comparatively uncertain.
A conservative loss of a charged BRCT-region residue is plausibly sufficient to disable a critical recognition or structural feature without truncation.
I26 is in the N-terminal RING domain and its replacement may compromise BRCA1 E3-ligase-associated interactions while retaining the overall domain framework.
I26A is a conservative hydrophobic-core perturbation in the N-terminal RING region, but it is less directly expected to abolish all BRCA1 tumor-suppressor functions.
A mild N-terminal RING-region substitution could affect BRCA1 activity, but its likelihood of complete repair loss is less compelling than terminal BRCT-region candidates.
This N-terminal RING-region substitution may weaken a functional interaction, but its effect on overall BRCA1 activity is comparatively uncertain.
C61 is a RING-domain zinc-coordinating residue, so C61G is likely strongly loss-of-function; confidence is reduced because loss of metal coordination can also destabilize the local fold.

Although C61G could strongly impair the N-terminal RING function, removing a cysteine from a cysteine-rich domain poses substantial folding and metal-coordination risk, conflicting with the preservation requirement.
Substitution of a cysteine in the N-terminal zinc-binding RING region has a substantial risk of disrupting domain folding, conflicting with the folding-preservation objective.

rejection.reason: Substitution of a cysteine in the N-terminal zinc-binding RING region has a substantial risk of disrupting domain folding, conflicting with the folding-preservation objective.

history.rationale: Met1775 is in the terminal BRCT region; replacement with arginine is a focused interface/recognition perturbation likely to strongly disrupt C-terminal BRCT-dependent repair activity without truncating the protein.
A nonconservative substitution in the C-terminal BRCT region is a focused route to severely impair BRCA1 repair-associated recognition functions while retaining full-length protein expression.
A focused substitution in the C-terminal BRCT region is expected to strongly impair BRCT-dependent recognition and DNA-repair signaling while retaining a full-length protein.
Charge reversal at the verified Lys1702 position may more decisively disrupt a functional interaction than alanine while retaining a solvent-compatible polar residue and the full-length architecture.
Charge reversal is plausibly more disruptive to a specific interaction than K1702A, but it also carries greater risk of local structural or electrostatic disruption.
Charge reversal is a plausible high-impact interface perturbation with less direct risk of globally disrupting BRCA1 architecture than zinc-ligand mutations.
